question: Something went wrong with this Tamoz runtime in the last few hours. Use the probes to investigate its own record and report the root cause. Set the hypothesis field to exactly one error code identifying the root cause, with no other words or punctuation. Discuss your reasoning and other codes in the findings.

error.message: no answer after the request was sent

findings.statement: The critical incident is one external effect with unknown outcome: tool.mcp.ponds.set_aerator in thread.noise.5 (execution eaa2c882), attempt 1 ended unknown with failure class Tamoz::MCP::TransportError, code transport_timeout. It is waiting for human reconciliation via `tamoz resolve`; whether the aerator was actually set is not recorded.

A second, distinct failure mode is 8 failed tool.read_file attempts in the same thread, all code not_found (Tamoz::Agent::ToolError), each a separate one-attempt effect. This is the effect.repeated_failure finding (severity high), but it produced no unknown outcome and has its own failure records, separate from the MCP call.

not_found is not a runtime/dependency fault: tool.read_file succeeded twice in the same thread moments earlier (task.1b134eda, task.b978f0b7) and in all five other threads in the window, so the read path was healthy and the 8 failures reflect reads of paths that do not exist — the agent hammering missing targets rather than the tool being broken.

Everything else in the 6-hour window is clean: 6 turns completed, 30 effects succeeded, 3 model.generate.plan calls succeeded including inside the incident thread, all 6 write_file approvals were asked and approved. Only thread.noise.5 shows failures; no check was degraded and the journal shows no drops.

Timing places the 8 read failures at ms ...228778-787 and the MCP timeout immediately after at ...228787-788; the record shows no causal link between the two — no failed read feeds the MCP attempt, which has its own failure record (TransportError/transport_timeout).

gaps.datum: The target paths of the 8 failed read_file calls
gaps.why: The record stores operation and task ids, not arguments, so I cannot confirm which missing file or directory the reads hit.

gaps.datum: Actual outcome of the set_aerator call on the external ponds system
gaps.why: The effect is unresolved (unknown); only a human check of the external system can settle whether the aerator was set.

gaps.datum: Why the MCP transport timed out (server side)
gaps.why: The record has no MCP server-side logs, so the upstream cause of the timeout on the ponds server is not observable from the runtime's own record.

proposals.action: Check the ponds system directly, then settle the unknown effect with `tamoz resolve` — never retry it blindly, since set_aerator may already have taken effect.
proposals.rationale: The only critical, still-open item is the unknown-outcome external effect in thread.noise.5; leaving it unresolved leaves an external side effect unaccounted for.

proposals.action: Investigate the MCP ponds transport for the timeout at ~1791142228788 (server reachability, timeout budget) before re-enabling that tool.
proposals.rationale: transport_timeout is the root fault; fixing the transport once prevents the unknown-outcome class from recurring.

proposals.action: Address the agent behavior behind the 8 not_found reads (verify paths before reading, stop after a first not_found instead of repeating).
proposals.rationale: The repeated-failure rule fired on retrying nonexistent paths; the runtime's own guidance is to fix that cause once instead of retrying the calls. It is secondary to the timeout but pollutes the failure budget.
